statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades 29,206.78, down 161.66 points or 0.55%, after opening at 28,890.93 on a 1.63% gap below the 29,368.44 previous close. The session range is 28,867.67 to 29,285.50. The session high has now stood unexceeded for more than an hour and price has eased roughly 79 points off it, which is the first sustained pause in the gap-recovery leg that held Tail in the watch band through the prior two hours. Cross-asset amplifiers continue to decay: VIX is 16.85 against an 18.17 session high, the 10-year yield is 4.961% and negative on the day after touching 5.012%, and WTI is near 101 after reaching 106.60 in Asian trade. Tail falls to 19 and maps to the low band.
recommendation: Tail at 19 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is retained at 19:00-20:00 UTC, covering the final cash hour and the closing auction, where an unresolved Middle East supply story and pre-FOMC positioning remain the identified conditional risks. The conditional path stays in the low band across the post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, with small uplifts at the Asian open and the European open where crude has typically repriced first. It re-enters the watch band only around Tuesday's US cash open at 13:00-14:00 UTC, which carries the highest conditional reading of the forecast at 21. Stress remains high at 68, reflecting an unresolved oil supply disruption and a policy decision on Wednesday, and continues to decay from 79 earlier today. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unchanged by this mapping.
headline: NDX holds 29,206.78 with the 29,285.50 session high unexceeded for over an hour and price 79 points below it; the first sustained retracement of the gap-recovery leg, alongside VIX decaying to 16.85 and the 10-year negative on the day, lowers Tail to 19 and the low band
body:
The extension that held this series in the watch band has stopped. As of the 19:25 UTC quote the Nasdaq-100 cash index is at 29,206.78, down 161.66 points or 0.55% against a 29,368.44 previous close, having opened at 28,890.93 on a 1.63% gap. The session range is 28,867.67 to 29,285.50. The high is the same high that was set more than an hour ago, and the index now trades about 79 points beneath it after easing from 29,242.44 at the prior assessment. For the first time today the recovery leg has given back ground and failed to extend.

That distinction is what moves this assessment. Through the middle of the session the one genuinely one-way element in the tape was a sequence of new session highs, which is the structure that denies a reverse or grid approach the mean reversion it depends on. That element is now absent: the market has retraced within the hour rather than extending, and the low at 28,867.67 set within minutes of the cash open remains untouched. Roughly 71% of the opening gap has been retraced and then partially given back, which is two-way behaviour rather than persistent directional efficiency.

The cross-asset picture confirms rather than contradicts the easing. VIX is 16.85, up 6.38% on the day but well off the 18.17 session high and close to its session low, so implied volatility is decaying rather than building. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.961%, down 1.4 basis points on the day, having traded as high as 5.012% earlier; the long end reaching 5% for the first time since 2023 was a headline earlier in the day, but yields are no longer an aligned amplifier because they are negative on the session. Crude has decayed furthest: Brent reached 108.49 and WTI 106.60 in Asian trade after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline following attacks, and both have since eased to roughly 105.6 and 101.2 respectively. A supply shock that spikes and then gives back most of the move is itself evidence that price discovery is orderly.

The underlying catalysts are nonetheless unresolved and keep Stress high. The East-West pipeline outage removes a route that carried several million barrels per day to Red Sea ports as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, and a projectile strike on a vessel in the Strait remains a live escalation channel. Separately, the AI complex weakened after Anthropic's chief executive published an essay urging the industry to slow frontier model development, which pressured Nvidia, AMD and SanDisk and weighed directly on index-heavy names. Markets price roughly 85% odds of a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC decision, the first of 2026, after core CPI came in slightly above expectations on Friday.

None of those are observed one-way price structure, and under this framework event importance, hawkish repricing and headline severity raise Stress and inform Confidence rather than Tail. Tail therefore falls to 19 and the low band, Stress eases to 68 and remains high, and Confidence is 87 on a current verified quote, a live 10-year yield, verified crude levels and a verified event calendar. The 2-year reference remains the 4.56% H.15 observation for September 10, and the shared Finviz context was stale and partial at collection, so both were used only as background.

The danger window is retained at 19:00-20:00 UTC for the closing auction. The conditional path holds in the low band overnight and reaches its highest reading of 21 at Tuesday's US cash open, where a second consecutive gap and an opening-auction continuation would be the specific mechanism capable of raising Tail again.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series began in the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band at 21:00 UTC as the AI-slowdown essay and the Middle East supply story developed, and held the watch band through the overnight and Asian sessions. It reached the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows under a trend-down mode, eased to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, and returned to the elevated band at 13:00 UTC as the first bounce faded into the cash open. From 14:00 UTC the series eased steadily as the opening gap was absorbed, reaching 18 and the low band at 16:00 UTC before returning to 21 at 17:00 and 18:00 UTC when the index extended to successive new session highs. Stress fell continuously from 79 at its peak to 71 by 18:00 UTC, and Confidence held between 87 and 89 for the whole US session.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built on an opening gap that was roughly 71% retraced and has now been partially given back, with the session high at 29,285.50 unexceeded for over an hour while VIX, the 10-year and crude all trade well off their session extremes. Conditional Tail holds at 19 through the final cash hour and the close, which form the retained 19:00-20:00 UTC danger window. It then settles between 17 and 18 across the CME maintenance halt, the post-halt reopen and the Asian session, with a small uplift at the Asian open where crude has typically repriced first on Middle East developments. The path lifts to 19 at the European open, holds in the low band through the European morning, and reaches its maximum of 21 at Tuesday's US cash open at 13:00 UTC, easing to 20 in the following hour. A second consecutive opening gap followed by continuation without a meaningful retracement is the specific mechanism that would raise Tail from there. The FOMC decision at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday falls outside this 24-hour window, though pre-event positioning is reflected in the final forecast hours.
